Marathon Petroleum fell 0.21% today to close at $472.69, but the real story is a reversal after a strong two-week run. Oil prices dropped today on hopes for a diplomatic resolution to Middle East tensions—U.S. crude fell below $102 a barrel—which took some steam out of the refining sector after weeks of geopolitical premium pushed prices higher. Refineries are running at 93.5% capacity with healthy fuel inventories, so there's less tailwind from supply tightness.

The stock is still up 9.3% over two weeks, a gain built on the escalation of Houthi attacks on shipping and Saudi infrastructure that sent Brent crude above $126. That premium evaporates fast if diplomacy gains traction; traders are betting cooler heads will prevail, which removes the risk premium that had boosted energy stocks earlier this month.
